title: Remove `path` from sched `params`
description:
`path` is being included in the `params` passed to the sched API, resulting in **path** being included as if it were session data.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/174085564-e33d48e4-062b-4ebb-93ef-c219a9131033.png)

I think it's from this line, which IIUC is no longer needed thanks to `sched_upsert()`.

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-conf-2022-program/blob/6c0d3964a9173cbf1bf950cb4e0d0deb19221097/sched.R#L97

I think the fix would be to push `path = NA` or `path = ""` once and then remove `path` from the line above.

title: Add TZ to talk times for virtual participation
description:
To make it easier for virtual participants to figure out talk times, could we add time zones to the talk times? 

Obviously it's all going to be in the same time zone, so another option would be for the talk times to be links to something like Time and Date, which would then show users their local time (or whatever time zone they desire). That API is quite simple, and the links would be easy enough to generate programmatically. For example, the first three talks in the table would become:

|Speakers                                                                                                                                                                  |Session                                                   |Talk                                                                                                                        |Day   |Time  |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----|:-----|
|[Julia Silge](assets/img/2022Conf/_talks/22301_julia-silge.jpeg), [Max Kuhn](assets/img/2022Conf/_talks/22301_max-kuhn.jpeg)                                              |[keynote](sessions/keynote/)                                       |[applied-machine-learning](sessions/keynote/applied-machine-learning.md)                                                             |Wed   |[09:00](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/fixedtime.html?msg=&iso=20220727T09&p1=263) |
|[Ryan E Wade](assets/img/2022Conf/_talks/22013_ryan-e-wade.jpg)                                                                                                           |[business-intelligence](sessions/business-intelligence/)           |[tidyverse-power-bi-match-made](sessions/business-intelligence/tidyverse-power-bi-match-made.md)                                     |Wed   |[11:00](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/fixedtime.html?msg=&iso=20220727T11&p1=263) |
|[James Blair](assets/img/2022Conf/_talks/22042_james-blair.jpg)                                                                                                           |[business-intelligence](sessions/business-intelligence/)           |[r-python-tableau-love-triangle](sessions/business-intelligence/r-python-tableau-love-triangle.md)                                   |Wed   |[11:20](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/fixedtime.html?msg=&iso=20220727T1120&p1=263) |


I just used the most basic feature for those links, the start time, talk title and duration could be added if so desired, e.g. for Applied Machine Learning (pretending it's two hours long): https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/fixedtime.html?msg=Applied+Machine+Learning&iso=20220727T09&p1=263&ah=2
